skills.name: Humanitarian and community services; reading an interview

note.text:
Humanitarian work helps people who suffer, for example after a flood, a fire or a war, or people who are poor or sick. Community service is work we do for free for the people around us: cleaning the market, visiting the sick, planting trees.
Picture talk: describe what people are doing (“A nurse is giving an injection”), then say why it helps.
In the interview, Dr Nkeng works in a village health centre every Saturday. With volunteers, nurses, students and the Red Cross, he gives free check-ups and vaccinations. Mama Ndum could not pay, but he treated her leg, and she was grateful.
Useful phrases: “I would like to help.” “Can I volunteer?” “Thank you for your help.”

worked_example.problem: {n}'s class wants to help old people in their quarter. Write two sentences about what they can do and why.
steps: Say the action: We can fetch water and clean the compound for old people who live alone.
Say why it helps: This is community service: it makes their life easier and shows we care.
worked_example.answer: We can fetch water and clean the compound for old people; it makes their life easier and shows we care.

cards.idea: Read the interview at a village health centre.
example: Reporter: Doctor, why do you work in the village health centre every Saturday?
Dr Nkeng: Many people here cannot travel to town. Volunteers and I give free check-ups and vaccinations.
Dr Nkeng: Nurses, students and the Red Cross. Some families donate food for the patients.
Reporter: Mama Ndum, what did the doctor do for you?
Mama Ndum: He treated my leg after my fall. I could not pay, but he helped me anyway. I am very grateful.

pick.q: When does Dr Nkeng work in the village?

pick.r: Many people cannot travel to town.
pick.y: He said many people cannot travel to town.

e: The Red Cross helps with the work.
pick.y: He said some families donate food for the patients.
She said: I am very grateful.

cards.idea: Humanitarian work helps people who suffer; community service is free work for the people around us.
example: After the flood, the Red Cross gave food and blankets.
Our class cleaned the market on Saturday.

cards.idea: In a picture talk, say what people are doing, then why it helps.
example: “This helps families who lost their homes.”

pick.q: Pupils clean the market every month for free. This is …
e: It is work, not a holiday.
pick.y: Free work for the people around us is community service.

pick.q: The Red Cross gives tents to families after a flood. This is …
e: It is help, not a lesson.
pick.y: Helping people who suffer after a disaster is humanitarian work.

pick.q: A doctor treats patients who cannot pay, for free. This is …

pick.r: A nurse is giving a baby a vaccine.
w: A nurse gives vaccines every Monday.
A nurse gave a vaccine yesterday.
A nurse will give a vaccine.
pick.y: Use the Present Continuous to describe a picture.

pick.r: Volunteers are carrying bags of rice.
pick.y: Use the Present Continuous to describe a picture.

w: Some pupils plant trees every year.
Some pupils are going to plant trees.
pick.y: Use the Present Continuous to describe a picture.

questions.prompt: In a picture talk, which sentence describes what is happening now?

pick.q: What does Dr Nkeng give with the volunteers?
e: He did not talk about books.
pick.y: He said: we give free check-ups and vaccinations.

pick.q: What did the doctor do for Mama Ndum?
e: She could not pay; he did not give money.
pick.y: She said: he treated my leg after my fall.

e: He did not name the police.
He did not name a bank.
He did not name a club.
pick.y: He said nurses, students and the Red Cross help him.

questions.prompt: One sentence is NOT true about the interview. Which one?

right.text: Dr Nkeng works in a village health centre.

wrong.text: Mama Ndum paid a lot of money for her treatment.
wrong.explain: She could not pay, but he helped her anyway.

wrong.text: Dr Nkeng works in the village every Monday.
The reporter treated Mama Ndum's leg.
wrong.explain: The doctor treated her leg; the reporter asked questions.
